settings.eyebrow: Stay safe, check before you drive
settings.subtext: Australia's strict 0.00% BAC limit for P-platers means guesswork can cost a licence. Confirm you're clear before turning the key.

settings.title: Mornings after
settings.body: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate — roughly 0.015% BAC per hour — and nothing speeds that up. Not coffee, not a cold shower, not eight hours of sleep. A big night can easily leave you over 0.00% well into the next morning, even if you feel completely fine and slept it off. The only way to know for sure before you drive to work, uni or sport is to actually check.

settings.title: Social & work events
settings.body: Casual drinks after work, a birthday, a work function — these are the moments where "I'm probably fine to drive" gets said the most, and where guesswork causes the most trouble. It's also where peer pressure makes it hardest to say no to one more. A quick, objective reading takes the guessing and the social awkwardness out of the decision entirely — no estimating, no relying on how you feel.

settings.title: P-plate rules
settings.body: Full licence holders get a small margin — 0.05% BAC. P1 and P2 drivers don't. The limit is a strict 0.00%, it applies 24/7 across every Australian state and territory, and it doesn't matter whether it's a Tuesday commute or a Saturday night out. The consequences also land harder on P-platers: an instant loss of licence, fines, and a real setback on the road to a full licence.

settings.title: Road trips
settings.body: Weekend getaways usually start with a few drinks the night before an early start, or a round at a stopover on the way. Regional and rural roads mean less traffic, but also less margin for error and often a longer wait for help if something goes wrong. Checking your BAC before you get back behind the wheel takes a few seconds and removes any doubt before a long drive with friends counting on you.
